cards.text: Jesus is back from the other side of the lake, and the crowd welcomes Him, because they had all been waiting for Him. ALL of them, friend. That's the kind of welcome I used to dream about from the back of a junk drawer.
Right then a man named Jairus, a synagogue leader, comes and falls at Jesus' feet. He begs Jesus to come to his house.

cards.question: Why is Jairus, the synagogue leader, begging Jesus to come to his house?

answers.text: His only son has a fever

cards.question: Jairus' only daughter is about ___ years old.

cards.text: So Jesus goes with him, and the crowds press in around Him like the bakery door on free-cookie day. Somewhere in that crush is a woman who has suffered from bleeding for twelve years.

cards.question: Trying to get better, the bleeding woman has spent all her money on ___.
After all those years of trying, one of the physicians finally heals the woman.

cards.text: So she comes up behind Jesus in the crowd. No speech, no introduction, she just reaches out.

cards.question: Coming up behind Jesus in the crowd, what does the woman touch?
When the woman touches Jesus' cloak, her bleeding stops ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “Who touched Me?” and they ALL deny it. It's the office break room after the last cookie goes missing: suddenly NOBODY knows ANYTHING.

cards.question: When Jesus asks who touched Him, Peter, one of His disciples, speaks up. What does Peter point out?

answers.text: The crowd is pressing against Him
Nobody is standing close to Him

cards.question: Jesus insists that someone touched Him. How does He know?

answers.text: Power has gone out from Him
He saw her reach for His cloak
Peter pointed her out to Him

cards.text: Now the woman sees she can't stay hidden, so she comes trembling and falls down before Him. I know that shake, friend, because it's the one I did every time the junk drawer rattled open.

cards.question: The woman whispers her story to Jesus alone, where nobody else can hear.
Jesus tells the woman what healed her. What is it?

cards.text: Jesus calls her “Daughter,” and then He tells her, “Go in peace.” Twelve years of physicians and empty pockets, and she walks off with PEACE.
While Jesus is still speaking, someone arrives from the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader. I bet Jairus has been counting every second this whole time.

cards.question: The messenger from Jairus' house has news for him. What is it?
The messenger tells Jairus to hurry and bring Jesus to the house.

cards.text: But Jesus overhears them. Jairus just heard his daughter is dead, and Jesus has something to say to him.

cards.question: Right after the news about his daughter, what does Jesus tell Jairus?

answers.text: Don't be afraid and just believe
Go home and comfort your wife
Wait here while I pray for her

cards.text: Jesus promises Jairus that she will be healed. Then they arrive at the house.

cards.question: At Jairus' house, Jesus lets the whole crowd come inside with Him.
Jesus lets in only His disciples Peter, John and James, plus the child's ___ and ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, everyone is weeping and mourning for the girl. Then Jesus says something nobody in that house expects.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the mourners about Jairus' daughter?

answers.text: She is not dead but asleep
She will wake in three days

cards.question: Knowing the girl is dead, the mourners ___ at Jesus.

cards.text: They laugh at Him, because they know she's dead. Friend, I once told jokes to a junk drawer full of rubber bands, and even THEY were a warmer room than this.
Then Jesus takes her by the hand.

cards.question: Holding the girl's hand, what does Jesus call out to her?
When Jesus calls to Jairus' daughter, she gets up at once.

cards.text: Her spirit returns, and she gets up at once. No groggy stretch, no snooze button, just UP.

cards.question: Jesus gives one more instruction about the girl. What does He say to do for her?

answers.text: Let her rest for a while

cards.text: Her parents are astounded. Me? I'd have fainted so hard my gold base would've hit the floor before I did.

cards.question: Jesus tells the girl's parents to go spread the news of what happened.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus is back "from the other side of the lake." That fact comes from the previous passage (Luke 8:22, 8:37), not from Luke 8:40, which only says "When Jesus returned." The card cites only Luke 8:40, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "The edge of His sleeve" is very close to the right answer "The fringe of His cloak." Both mean the edge of His clothing, and a baker could argue it's right. It also isn't a real detail from elsewhere in the Bible, as a which-thing question needs.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 5 already told the baker that the crowds press in around Jesus (Luke 8:42). That rules out the wrong answer "Nobody is standing close to Him" and practically hands over the right answer, so only one real choice is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The two-blank card "the child's ___ and ___" sets father as blank 1 and mother as blank 2. The other order, mother and father, is just as true, and a baker who picks it could argue they're right.
findings.question: When two blanks can be filled in either order, should both orders count as right, or should the card be rewritten so each blank has only one possible answer?

findings.problem: "Nobody in that house" puts the weeping mourners inside the house. Card 8 just said Jesus let only Peter, John, James and the parents go in. Luke 8:52 doesn't say where the mourners are, so the card shouldn't place them, and the way it does contradicts the card before it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Something nobody in that house expects" states what the mourners think as fact. It isn't marked as Papa Dorin's own guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The story card repeats the answer that card 11 just asked about ("They laugh at Him, because they know she's dead") and cites the same verse. It adds nothing new from the passage, so it's a recap.

The joke's comparison doesn't match the action. In the passage, the people are mocking Jesus by laughing at Him. The joke is about a cold audience that doesn't laugh, which is the opposite. The setup also casts Jesus as a comedian bombing in a tough room, which puts His words in the place of a joke. The backstory also says that in the drawer, Dorin "didn't joke at all" for a while, and nothing in it says he told jokes to the rubber bands.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "I'd have fainted so hard my gold base would've hit the floor before I did" is a confusing picture. It needs explaining, and it suggests the base and Dorin could separate, but the base always comes with him.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
